cards.front: adaptation
cards.back: A feature or behaviour that helps a living thing survive in its habitat.
cards.say: adaptation. A feature or behaviour that helps a living thing survive in its habitat.

cards.front: habitat
cards.back: The place where a plant or animal lives.
cards.say: habitat. The place where a plant or animal lives.

cards.front: How is a camel adapted to the desert?
cards.back: Its hump stores fat, it has wide feet for walking on sand and long eyelashes to keep sand out of its eyes.
cards.say: How is a camel adapted to the desert? Its hump stores fat, it has wide feet for walking on sand and long eyelashes to keep sand out of its eyes.

cards.front: How is a cactus adapted to the desert?
cards.back: It stores water in a thick stem. It has spines instead of leaves, so it loses less water.
cards.say: How is a cactus adapted to the desert? It stores water in a thick stem. It has spines instead of leaves, so it loses less water.

cards.front: How is a polar bear adapted to the cold?
cards.back: It has thick fur, a thick layer of fat to keep warm and white fur for camouflage in snow.
cards.say: How is a polar bear adapted to the cold? It has thick fur, a thick layer of fat to keep warm and white fur for camouflage in snow.

cards.front: camouflage
cards.back: Colours or patterns that help an animal blend in with its surroundings.
cards.say: camouflage. Colours or patterns that help an animal blend in with its surroundings.

cards.front: blubber
cards.back: A thick layer of fat under the skin of seals and whales. It keeps them warm in cold water.
cards.say: blubber. A thick layer of fat under the skin of seals and whales. It keeps them warm in cold water.

cards.front: Why do penguins huddle together?
cards.back: Sharing body heat keeps them warm in the cold wind.
cards.say: Why do penguins huddle together? Sharing body heat keeps them warm in the cold wind.

cards.front: hibernation
cards.back: A deep sleep that some animals have in winter, to save energy when food is hard to find.
cards.say: hibernation. A deep sleep that some animals have in winter, to save energy when food is hard to find.

cards.front: migration
cards.back: A long journey that animals make to another place at certain times of year, to find food or a warmer place.
cards.say: migration. A long journey that animals make to another place at certain times of year, to find food or a warmer place.

cards.front: How do rainforest leaves cope with heavy rain?
cards.back: Many have pointed tips, called drip tips, so water runs off quickly.
cards.say: How do rainforest leaves cope with heavy rain? Many have pointed tips, called drip tips, so water runs off quickly.

cards.front: How is a water lily adapted to life on a pond?
cards.back: Its leaves are wide and flat and float on the water, so they catch sunlight.
cards.say: How is a water lily adapted to life on a pond? Its leaves are wide and flat and float on the water, so they catch sunlight.

cards.front: nocturnal
cards.back: Active at night. Many desert animals are nocturnal, to avoid the heat of the day.
cards.say: nocturnal. Active at night. Many desert animals are nocturnal, to avoid the heat of the day.

cards.front: How do predators' eyes help them hunt?
cards.back: Eyes at the front of the head let them judge distance well.
cards.say: How do predators' eyes help them hunt? Eyes at the front of the head let them judge distance well.

cards.front: What other adaptations help predators?
cards.back: Sharp teeth and claws, speed and strong senses of smell, sight or hearing.
cards.say: What other adaptations help predators? Sharp teeth and claws, speed and strong senses of smell, sight or hearing.

cards.front: How do prey animals' eyes help them survive?
cards.back: Eyes on the sides of the head give a wide view, so they can spot predators coming.
cards.say: How do prey animals' eyes help them survive? Eyes on the sides of the head give a wide view, so they can spot predators coming.

cards.front: How does camouflage help prey animals?
cards.back: It makes them hard for predators to see.
cards.say: How does camouflage help prey animals? It makes them hard for predators to see.

cards.front: How is an owl adapted for hunting at night?
cards.back: It has large eyes, excellent hearing, silent feathers and sharp talons.
cards.say: How is an owl adapted for hunting at night? It has large eyes, excellent hearing, silent feathers and sharp talons.

cards.front: How is a fish adapted to live in water?
cards.back: It has a streamlined body, fins for swimming and gills for breathing.
cards.say: How is a fish adapted to live in water? It has a streamlined body, fins for swimming and gills for breathing.

cards.front: How is a mole adapted to living underground?
cards.back: It has strong front claws for digging and small eyes because it lives in the dark.
cards.say: How is a mole adapted to living underground? It has strong front claws for digging and small eyes because it lives in the dark.

cards.front: Why does a giraffe have a long neck?
cards.back: It can reach leaves high up in trees that other animals cannot reach.
cards.say: Why does a giraffe have a long neck? It can reach leaves high up in trees that other animals cannot reach.

cards.front: Why do deciduous trees lose their leaves in winter?
cards.back: It saves water and energy when it is cold and there is little light.
cards.say: Why do deciduous trees lose their leaves in winter? It saves water and energy when it is cold and there is little light.

cards.front: Why does an Arctic fox have small ears?
cards.back: Small ears lose less body heat in the cold.
cards.say: Why does an Arctic fox have small ears? Small ears lose less body heat in the cold.

cards.front: Why does a desert fox have big ears?
cards.back: Big ears lose heat easily, which helps keep it cool in the hot desert.
cards.say: Why does a desert fox have big ears? Big ears lose heat easily, which helps keep it cool in the hot desert.
